pois.name: One World Trade Center
pois.description: The Western Hemisphere's tallest building (541.3m, symbolic height of 1,776 ft for 1776). One World Observatory on floors 100–102 offers a 360° view of greater New York.

pois.name: 9/11 Memorial & Museum
pois.description: Michael Arad's Reflecting Absence: two acre-wide pools set in the exact footprints of the Twin Towers, framed by 400 white swamp oaks. Open year-round.

pois.name: Brooklyn Bridge
pois.description: John Roebling's 1883 Gothic-tower suspension bridge — the world's first wire cable suspension bridge. The wooden promenade above traffic is a 30-min walk to Brooklyn.

pois.name: Charging Bull
pois.description: Arturo Di Modica's 3.2-tonne bronze sculpture (1989), placed illegally outside the NYSE as a 'guerrilla gift'. The most photographed sculpture in New York.

pois.name: Battery Park
pois.description: Manhattan's southern tip. The ferry to the Statue of Liberty departs from Castle Clinton here. Ellis Island and the Governors Island ferry also depart from the Battery.
